name: A Discrete Synthetic Benchmark for PCA-Ridge and Reference-Ray 3-D Velocity Reconstruction from First-Arrival Travel Times
description: Reproducibility archive for the article “A Discrete Synthetic Benchmark for PCA-Ridge and Reference-Ray 3-D Velocity Reconstruction from First-Arrival Travel Times”. We present a discrete synthetic benchmark for reconstructing 3-D P-wave velocity from first-arrival travel times. The corpus has 250 geological targets in five families, 384 observations each, and a 175/37/38 target-atomic split. Travel times use a rectilinear Fast-Sweeping calculation on a 1.25-km grid; evaluation uses direct analytic velocity at 2.5-km cell centers. Validation-only selection chose a node-native full-input principal component analysis ridge (PCA-ridge) with one component and ridge penalty 1000, and a direct-cell selection agreed. Across 38 test targets the apparent workflow ordering depends materially on the declared contracts: the declared identifier-ordered workflow gives direct-cell root-mean-square error 0.3534 km/s, geometry-canonical re-ordering with penalty reselection gives 0.3104 km/s, and a cell-native parameterization gives 0.2612 km/s, against 0.2718 km/s for the intentionally non-equivalent Reference-ray baseline. The declared complete-workflow comparison is a paired difference of +0.0817 km/s (95% percentile-bootstrap interval [+0.0492,+0.1201] km/s) favoring the baseline, retrospectively designated and descriptive.
